q: Covalent bonding usually occurs between _____.
e: Covalent bonding usually occurs between non-metals. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: A covalent bond is the electrostatic attraction between the nuclei of the atoms and the _____ electrons.
e: A covalent bond is the electrostatic attraction between the nuclei of the atoms and the shared electrons. Core electrons stay inner and do not bond.

q: When hydrogen atoms are approaching, there is a repulsive force between the electrons since like charges _____.
e: When hydrogen atoms are approaching, there is a repulsive force between the electrons since like charges repel. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: There is an optimum distance between two nuclei called the bond length where net attractive forces are _____.
e: There is an optimum distance between two nuclei called the bond length where net attractive forces are maximised. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In single covalent bonds, only _____ pair of electrons is shared between two atoms.
e: In single covalent bonds, only one pair of electrons is shared between two atoms. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: A double bond is formed by sharing _____ pairs of electrons between two atoms.
e: A double bond is formed by sharing two pairs of electrons between two atoms. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The higher the number of bonded electrons, the stronger the attraction and the _____ the bond length.
e: The higher the number of bonded electrons, the stronger the attraction and the shorter the bond length. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The bond length of the single bond is the longest, followed by the double bond and _____ bond.
e: The bond length of the single bond is the longest, followed by the double bond and triple bond. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The bond strength of the _____ bond is the highest, followed by the double bond and single bond.
e: The bond strength of the triple bond is the highest, followed by the double bond and single bond. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: A coordinate bond is characterised by the fact that the two shared electrons are both donated by _____ of the participating atoms.
e: A coordinate bond is characterised by the fact that the two shared electrons are both donated by one of the participating atoms. In a coordinate, or dative, bond one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

q: A coordinate bond is formed when one of the participating atoms possesses an unshared pair of electrons known as a _____.
e: A coordinate bond is formed when one of the participating atoms possesses an unshared pair of electrons known as a lone pair. In a coordinate, or dative, bond one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

q: A coordinate bond is expressed as an arrow which indicates the direction in which the electrons are _____.
e: A coordinate bond is expressed as an arrow which indicates the direction in which the electrons are donated. In a coordinate, or dative, bond one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

q: The ammonia molecule possesses a lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom; it can be donated to a hydrogen ion to produce the _____ ion.
e: The ammonia molecule possesses a lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom; it can be donated to a hydrogen ion to produce the ammonium ion. A lone pair sits on an atom and is not shared in a bond, but it still takes space and can bend the shape.

q: A water molecule can react with a hydrogen ion through a coordinate bond, giving a _____ ion.
e: A water molecule can react with a hydrogen ion through a coordinate bond, giving a hydronium ion. In a coordinate, or dative, bond one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

q: Molecules with incomplete octets are called _____ molecules.
e: Molecules with incomplete octets are called electron-deficient molecules. An electron-deficient molecule does not have enough valence electrons for an octet on the central atom, like BF3.

q: An ammonia molecule can combine with boron trifluoride using a coordinate bond to form an _____.
e: An ammonia molecule can combine with boron trifluoride using a coordinate bond to form an adduct. In a coordinate, or dative, bond one atom donates both electrons of the shared pair.

q: In carbon monoxide, the CO molecule has a triple bond that consists of two covalent bonds and one _____ bond.
e: In carbon monoxide, the CO molecule has a triple bond that consists of two covalent bonds and one coordinate bond. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: In drawing Lewis structures, for ions, it is necessary to add electrons to account for negative charges, and _____ electrons to account for positive charges.
e: In drawing Lewis structures, for ions, it is necessary to add electrons to account for negative charges, and subtract electrons to account for positive charges. A Lewis acid accepts an electron pair and a Lewis base donates one.

q: The central atom in an electron-deficient molecule has valence electrons of less than _____.
e: The central atom in an electron-deficient molecule has valence electrons of less than 8. An electron-deficient molecule does not have enough valence electrons for an octet on the central atom, like BF3.

q: The central atom in an expanded valence shell molecule has valence electrons of more than _____.
e: The central atom in an expanded valence shell molecule has valence electrons of more than 8. Valence electrons sit in the outermost shell, and those are the electrons that actually form bonds.

q: The molecular shape can be predicted by using the Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory, also known as the _____ model.
e: The molecular shape can be predicted by using the Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory, also known as the VSEPR model. Aufbau fills lower-energy orbitals first.

q: The repulsive interaction of electron pairs increases in the order of bonding pair-bonding pair < lone pair-bonding pair < _____.
e: The repulsive interaction of electron pairs increases in the order of bonding pair-bonding pair < lone pair-bonding pair < lone pair-lone pair. Core-core: core electrons stay inner and do not bond.

q: The lone pairs of electrons in a molecule occupy _____ space compared with the bonding pairs of electrons.
e: The lone pairs of electrons in a molecule occupy more space compared with the bonding pairs of electrons. A bonding pair is the electron pair shared between two atoms in a covalent bond.

q: A triatomic molecule ($AX_2$ type) with only two bonding pairs without lone pairs has a _____ shape.
e: A triatomic molecule (AX2 type) with only two bonding pairs without lone pairs has a linear shape. A bonding pair is the electron pair shared between two atoms in a covalent bond.

q: In the $CO_2$ molecule, there are four bonding pairs (two double bonds) without lone pairs, hence the shape of $CO_2$ is _____.
e: In the CO2 molecule, there are four bonding pairs (two double bonds) without lone pairs, hence the shape of CO2 is linear. A bonding pair is the electron pair shared between two atoms in a covalent bond.

q: The $AX_3$ type molecule without lone pairs has a _____ shape.
e: The AX3 type molecule without lone pairs has a triangular planar shape. A lone pair sits on an atom and is not shared in a bond, but it still takes space and can bend the shape.

q: The $AX_2E$ type molecule, where E represents a lone pair, has a _____ shape.
e: The AX2E type molecule, where E represents a lone pair, has a bent/V-shaped shape. A lone pair sits on an atom and is not shared in a bond, but it still takes space and can bend the shape.

q: The $AX_4$ type molecule without lone pairs has a _____ shape.
e: The AX4 type molecule without lone pairs has a tetrahedral shape. A lone pair sits on an atom and is not shared in a bond, but it still takes space and can bend the shape.

q: The $AX_3E$ type molecule has a _____ shape.
e: The AX3E type molecule has a trigonal pyramidal shape. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In a diamond, each carbon atom is joined to _____ other carbon atoms by strong covalent bonds.
e: In a diamond, each carbon atom is joined to four other carbon atoms by strong covalent bonds. A covalent bond is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.

q: In the case of graphite, each layer is formed with _____ rings of carbon atoms.
e: In the case of graphite, each layer is formed with hexagonal rings of carbon atoms. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: There are weak _____ forces between the layers of graphite.
e: There are weak van der Waals forces between the layers of graphite. Van der Waals forces are weak intermolecular attractions, including dipole-dipole, ion-dipole, and London forces.

q: In contrast to diamond, graphite has free-moving electrons in each layer, that is why graphite can conduct _____.
e: In contrast to diamond, graphite has free-moving electrons in each layer, that is why graphite can conduct electricity. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Silicon(IV) oxide, $SiO_2$, is an example of a giant _____ molecule.
e: Silicon(IV) oxide, SiO2, is an example of a giant covalent molecule. Covalent bonding is a shared pair of electrons between atoms.
